title: Redwood x Skylink Cloud - Partner intro & discovery
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Skylink Cloud. Covered Skylink's go-to-market motion, hardware footprint (edge + regionals), common customers, technical constraints around private deployments/VPC, and potential integration patterns (marketplace listing, joint benchmarks, referral agreement). Discussed Redwood Dedicated vs Private options, latency/cost tradeoffs, and next steps: share partner deck, schedule technical deep-dive with infra team, and propose a pilot outline.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-31 15:00 PST — duration 52m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood Partnerships); Priya Nair (Skylink Head of Partnerships), Luca Romano (Infra Lead), Anika Shah (Edge PM), Samir Patel (Security)

Summary (auto): quick partner intro, high level infra + go-to-market, identify overlap in enterprise customers, agree next steps for tech deep dive and pilot.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, happy new year early, thanks for joining, i think we're all on the same call, quick intros?
[00:06] Priya Nair: yeah hi, priya from skylink, i run partnerships, thanks for setting this up, excited to chat.
[00:10] Carlos Ruiz: carlos here, i'm the solutions engineer at redwood, i'll cover the tech bits, hi!
[00:14] Luca Romano: luca from infra, uh, we run our regional edge clusters and some colo partnerships.
[00:19] Jordan Lee: jordan, partnerships at redwood, i'll be helping coordinate go-to-market.
[00:22] Anika Shah: anika, product for edge and marketplace integrations; curious about how the developer experience will look.
[00:28] Samir Patel: samir, security architect, quick heads up — we care about KMS integration, audit logs, and data residency.

[00:35] Maya Chen: great, thanks — objective for today's 45-ish minute chat is just a discovery: understand skylink's infra + partners, share a little about redwood offerings (hosted/dedicated/private), and surface integration options that make sense.
[00:48] Priya Nair: cool, so high level from our side: we operate a distributed cloud focused on low-latency regional inference — think telco partners, retailers with edge sites. We sell marketplace listings and also do managed deployments for select customers. We're exploring stronger partner programs around LLM inference because many of our customers ask for turnkey solutions.
[01:08] Maya Chen: perfect, that's very aligned. quick high level from redwood: we do hosted API, dedicated reserved pools for customers, and private deployments for VPC/on-prem use cases. Our core differentiator is serving runtime optimizations — batching, KV cache, kernel selection — and unified tooling so the same API and ops surface works across those deployment modes.
[01:36] Luca Romano: when you say private, do you mean full control plane in our VPC? like, we want to host and manage keys — HSM/KMS — as a hard requirement.
[01:44] Carlos Ruiz: yeah we have a private offering where the control plane can be customer-managed; integration with your KMS or customer HSM is supported. there are a couple of deployment patterns: fully air-gapped on prem, or hosted control plane with VPC peering. sometimes the transcript will say "redwood privat" cause the auto transcriber wobbles.
[02:02] Samir Patel: are audit logs and SSO supported out of the box? our customers require SOC2-level logs and SAML SSO.
[02:09] Maya Chen: absolutely — we offer audit logs, RBAC, SAML/SSO integrations, plus SOC 2 compliance for hosted. for private we recommend customers bring their own compliance artifacts and we integrate with their identity provider.
[02:23] Anika Shah: on the marketplace side, how lightweight is the integration? can we list a managed endpoint that our customers spin up, or do you expect a full onboarding for each customer?
[02:34] Jordan Lee: good Q. we support both: a simple listing that points to a hosted redwood endpoint, or deeper integration where we ship a private package into your infra so customers can self-provision in their region. the latter needs a bit more ops work.
[02:49] Priya Nair: what's the typical latency profile for dedicated pools vs private on-prem? a lot of our customers are latency sensitive, <50ms token is ideal for some use cases.
[02:58] Carlos Ruiz: it's workload dependent; for short context chat generation on modern LLMs on-prem we can get pretty low single-digit token latencies with NVLink infra and optimized kernels. but realistic numbers: for 8k context, often 20–60ms token depending on batch. also batching helps throughput but buys latency tradeoffs. we should do a benchmark for your typical prompt distributions.
[03:20] Luca Romano: you mentioned kernel selection and kv caching — curious how that works in multi-tenant environments, will cache privacy be an issue?
[03:28] Carlos Ruiz: we do prefix/KV caching with strict tenant isolation. i.e., caches are per-customer or per-endpoint depending on config; for marketplace managed endpoints we'd default to per-tenant isolation. some transcriber notes might say "K V cash" instead of KV cache, apologies.
[03:41] Samir Patel: and encryption at rest? key rotation?
[03:44] Maya Chen: yes, encryption at rest, rotation via KMS, and you can bring your own keys. for private deployments you can integrate with your HSM.

[03:58] Priya Nair: moving to commercial model, does redwood do revenue share for marketplace listings or referral fees?
[04:04] Jordan Lee: we have flexible models — revenue share for marketplace listings, referral credits, or reseller arrangements. typically we tailor it to the scale and the partner contribution (e.g., co-marketing, joint sales motion).
[04:16] Priya Nair: ok. our simplest starting point would be a referral + co-marketing agreement and then pilot a managed endpoint offering.

[04:25] Maya Chen: sounds good. on the technical side, what would you need from us to scope a pilot?
[04:30] Anika Shah: we need an installable package or terraform module, docs for lifecycle management, and a simple self-service on/off ramp for customers. also we want a small benchmark showing cost per token in our infra compared to hosted.
[04:42] Carlos Ruiz: we can provide a helm/terraform package for private deployment, plus a benchmark harness. i'd like to schedule a technical deep dive with luca's infra team to capture cluster specs — GPU models, network topology, and colocation constraints.
[04:55] Luca Romano: perfect; we run a mix of A100s and upcoming L5-class accelerators at select edges, plus some AMD MI250 in central regions. network varies by site — some are 1Gb metro links.
[05:08] Carlos Ruiz: perfect, that helps — LPs like quantization profiles matter for MI/AMD; we'll need to validate kernel availability.
[05:16] Priya Nair: security — our compliance team will need SOC2 docs, any pen test reports, and assurance on data deletion policies.
[05:25] Maya Chen: we will share our compliance pack and SOC2 report for hosted; for private we can provide the relevant integration docs and recommend wording for customer contracts.

[05:37] Priya Nair: curious — who would own the support? if we co-sell a managed endpoint, do we triage first line or do you handle support?
[05:45] Jordan Lee: usually partners who run the managed instance do first-line support with escalation to redwood for product-level issues; we can discuss joint SLA.

[05:55] Anika Shah: any red flags around licensing for models? do you bring models or do customers bring their own?
[06:01] Carlos Ruiz: we support both. we have a model catalog with curated open models and verified performance profiles; customers can also bring licensed models — we handle versioning, rollouts. sometimes open model names get butchered in transcripts, e.g., "megalo" for some model names.

[06:15] (brief crosstalk)
[06:18] Priya Nair: timeline-wise, we're aiming to have a pilot option live in Q1 to show at an upcoming telco trade show in mid-march.
[06:26] Maya Chen: okay Q1 pilot timeline is feasible. immediate next step: share partner deck and a proposed pilot scope; technical deep dive with luca and team next week ideally.

[06:40] Carlos Ruiz: i'll follow up with a questionnaire to capture GPU types, connectivity, and sample prompt distributions — even a spreadsheet with typical prompt lengths helps.
[06:50] Samir Patel: we'll also need a checklist for security integrations (SAML, KMS provisioning).

[07:00] Priya Nair: what about competitive landscape? we've been evaluating aws bedrock, lambda labs, and some boutique inference providers.
[07:08] Maya Chen: noted; we typically highlight deterministic latency, cost controls, and unified ops across environments — those are often differentiators vs managed cloud endpoints.

[07:20] Jordan Lee: also, we can run a quick pilot benchmark vs one or two competitors if you want to include that in the trade show materials.

[07:30] Priya Nair: yes that would be helpful, timeline dependent.

[07:35] Maya Chen: cool — let me recap: redwood to share partner deck, SOC2 and compliance docs, terraform/helm package for private deployment, and a benchmark harness template; carlos to schedule infra deep-dive with luca; jordan to follow up on commercial partnership templates; skylink to provide sample customer prompt distributions and security contact for SAML/KMS.
[07:56] Priya Nair: sounds good, i'll get the prompts and security contact by monday.

[08:02] Anika Shah: one more minor question — do you support streaming responses and function/tool calling in your API? some of our retail customers need streaming for interactive experiences.
[08:11] Carlos Ruiz: yes we support streaming, tool calling, and structured outputs. the runtime is optimized for that. random transcriber artifact: sometimes "streaming" becomes "stream ring".

[08:20] Maya Chen: ok if no other questions we'll close with next steps and action items. thanks everyone for the time.
[08:27] Priya Nair: thanks, appreciate it.

End of transcript.

Notes about transcription quality: medium — some proper nouns and acronyms may be mis-transcribed, occasional filler words and overlapping talk.
